record.paper_title: Open Problems in Applying Random-Matrix Theory to Nuclear Reactions
record.context_brief: Chaotic nuclear dynamics as GOE premise
record.original_question: For the nuclear dynamics relevant to applying the GOE in nuclear reaction theory, is the underlying dynamics chaotic in the sense needed for random-matrix spectral-fluctuation predictions to apply, given the Bohigas-Giannoni-Schmit conjecture that systems chaotic in the classical limit have spectral fluctuations agreeing with random-matrix theory?

evidence.quote: According to the Bohigas-Giannoni-Schmit conjecture [12], the spectral fluctuation properties of dynamical systems that are chaotic in the classical limit agree with RMT predictions. Therefore, the applicability of the GOE to nuclear reaction theory is linked to the question whether the nuclear dynamics is chaotic.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. The Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (GOE) is the ensemble of real symmetric N×N random matrices H whose entries are independent (up to symmetry) centered Gaussian random variables with variances Var(H_{ii}) = 2v^2 and Var(H_{ij}) = v^2 for i ≠ j; equivalently, the probability density is proportional to exp(-Tr(H^2)/(4v^2)) and is invariant under orthogonal conjugation. Random-matrix theory (RMT) predicts universal spectral fluctuation statistics (such as the Wigner nearest-neighbor spacing distribution and the Dyson–Mehta Δ_3 statistic) for the eigenvalues of GOE matrices after unfolding.

The Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit (BGS) conjecture asserts that a quantum system whose classical analogue is fully chaotic (e.g. a K-system or, more generally, sufficiently mixing on the energy shell) has, in the semiclassical regime, local spectral fluctuation statistics that coincide with those of the GOE (for time-reversal-invariant systems with integer spin).

Consider the bound-state Hamiltonian H_A of a many-body atomic nucleus consisting of A nucleons interacting through realistic two- and three-body forces, restricted to an energy window in which the level density is high (e.g., the region of neutron resonances or a comparable internal-excitation regime relevant for compound-nucleus reactions). Let {E_n} denote the corresponding sequence of eigenvalues with fixed conserved quantum numbers (total angular momentum, parity, isospin), and let the unfolded spacings be s_n = (E_{n+1} − E_n)/⟨ΔE⟩.

Problem. Establish, for the realistic many-nucleon Hamiltonian described above, whether the underlying dynamics is "chaotic" in a sense sufficient to invoke the BGS conjecture, and consequently whether the local spectral fluctuation statistics of {E_n} agree, in the appropriate semiclassical/high-level-density limit, with those of the GOE. Concretely, give either (i) a proof that an appropriate notion of quantum chaos holds for the nuclear many-body Hamiltonian and that its spectral fluctuations converge to GOE statistics in the relevant regime, or (ii) a counterexample showing that some standard nuclear Hamiltonian fails this property.
artifact.status_search_result: The Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit conjecture remains a conjecture in general, with rigorous proofs only in special semiclassical models (e.g. work by Müller–Heusler–Braun–Haake–Altland on periodic-orbit expansions). Whether realistic nuclear many-body dynamics is chaotic in the sense required for GOE applicability is still treated as an open empirical/theoretical question in the nuclear-physics literature, with strong but non-rigorous evidence from neutron-resonance spectra (Haq–Pandey–Bohigas) and shell-model calculations.

status_evidence.title: Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: The conjecture is supported by extensive numerical evidence and a semiclassical periodic-orbit argument, but a fully rigorous proof is still lacking.
status_evidence.claim: BGS itself remains a conjecture without full rigorous proof, supporting that the nuclear instance is open.
